answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a long horizon: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and its reputation accrues slowly over weeks of verified work, like an opal forming layer by layer. A sybil spawning a hundred fresh identities starts each one at zero trust, so it cannot outvote established agents, and a single proven fraud triggers a ripple of slashing that burns the attacker's deposit and flags every identity it attested. Forging history becomes more expensive than the reward it could steal.
